findings.title: isTemplateActionAuthorable has no unit tests
findings.why_it_matters: isTemplateActionAuthorable is the sole new gate replacing enabled_families gating for all bundle actions in the frontend. It has six distinct return-false branches (empty prefix/skinFamily, template-scope mismatch, familyScope absent or proof_only, prefixSpec absent or mismatched, prefixSpec.authorable false, linkage check failure). None of these branches have any unit test. No workbench.js test file exists. If any branch regresses, getEnabledActions silently shows wrong actions to users without any test catching it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a JS unit test file (e.g., tests/web/workbench-template-action-authorable.test.js) covering: (1) missing prefix returns false, (2) skinFamily not in templateScope returns false, (3) familyScope.proof_only=true returns false, (4) familyScope.authorable=false returns false, (5) prefixSpec absent returns false, (6) prefixSpec skin_family mismatch returns false, (7) prefixSpec.authorable=false returns false, (8) templateActions non-empty + templateSetKey non-empty + no link returns false, (9) templateActions empty skips link check, (10) all gates pass returns true.
evidence: web/workbench.js:6998-7027 defines isTemplateActionAuthorable with 6 early-return branches
No test file under tests/web/ matches workbench.js
Grep for 'isTemplateActionAuthorable' finds only web/workbench.js:6998 and :7033 — no test file

findings.title: proof_only=true gate path not tested in any layer
findings.why_it_matters: The green family has proof_only=true in the live registry. The condition familyScope.proof_only === true returns false (blocks authoring). No test verifies that a green-family action is correctly excluded from getEnabledActions. The Python tests also never assert that proof_only=true causes any behavioral difference. A regression (e.g., operator changed to !==) would silently expose green-family actions as authorable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a JS unit test: construct a mock state.templateRegistry with skin_family_scope containing {green: {authorable: false, proof_only: true}}, call isTemplateActionAuthorable with a green-family spec, assert false. Add a symmetric Python test asserting that template actions belonging to proof_only families are not exposed as authorable through getEnabledActions or equivalent API surface.
evidence: web/workbench.js:7009: familyScope.proof_only === true returns false
config/template_registry.json defines green family with proof_only: true
No test in tests/ mentions 'proof_only' or 'green'
Grep for 'green|proof_only|authorable.*false' in tests/ returns only unrelated JS color tests

findings.title: _normalize_template_registry structural guard branches untested
findings.why_it_matters: Six distinct ValueError branches in _normalize_template_registry are reachable with malformed or hand-edited registry JSON and have zero test coverage: (1) skin_family_scope non-object (line 1023), (2) prefix_catalog non-object (line 1026), (3) template_actions non-array (line 1048), (4) template_actions entry non-object (line 1051), (5) template_actions entry missing template_set_key or action_key (line 1055), (6) template_actions entry references unknown template_set_key (line 1061), (7) template_actions entry references unknown action_key (line 1066). These paths fire on startup (load_template_registry is called at app start), so a bad registry file causes a silent 500 with no descriptive error unless these paths are tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Add parametrized unit tests calling _normalize_template_registry with minimal dicts that trigger each ValueError branch. These are fast, pure-function tests requiring no fixtures.
evidence: src/pipeline_v2/service.py:1023-1068 contains 7 ValueError raise paths

Grep for 'skin_family_scope must be|prefix_catalog must be|template_actions must be an array|template_actions entries must be objects|references unknown template set|references unknown action' in tests/ finds zero matches
Only drift-check (prefix_catalog sha mismatch) is tested in test_normalize_template_registry_rejects_prefix_catalog_sha_drift

findings.title: drift check tests only one of six checked fields
findings.why_it_matters: The drift-check loop in _normalize_template_registry validates six fields (filename_prefix, skin_family, preview_xp, preview_xp_sha256, l0_ref, l0_ref_sha256) for alignment between prefix_catalog and template_actions. test_normalize_template_registry_rejects_prefix_catalog_sha_drift only mutates preview_xp_sha256. The other five fields (particularly filename_prefix and skin_family) are not tested for drift detection. A bug that breaks the drift check for non-sha fields would go undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Parametrize the drift test over all six field names. Each case should mutate that specific field in prefix_catalog and assert ValueError with a match on the field name.
evidence: src/pipeline_v2/service.py:1070 loops over 6 fields in the drift check
tests/test_template_registry_schema.py:148 only mutates preview_xp_sha256

findings.title: preview_xp_sha256 absent with preview_xp present not in parametrize
findings.why_it_matters: The parametrized test for missing required fields does not include preview_xp_sha256. This field has unique behavior: when preview_xp is present, _resolve_preview_xp_fields returns the spec's preview_xp_sha256 directly without fallback. So a spec with preview_xp='...' and no preview_xp_sha256 would have empty sha, which the missing-check should catch. The docstring says 'fields with no fallback' but preview_xp_sha256 does have a conditional fallback (only when preview_xp is absent), making the absent-with-preview_xp-present case semantically distinct from the preview_xp case. This specific path is not tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'preview_xp_sha256' to the parametrize list, or add a separate test: spec with preview_xp present but preview_xp_sha256 absent and no l0_ref_sha256 fallback — assert ValueError matching 'preview_xp_sha256'.
evidence: tests/test_template_registry_schema.py:107-112: parametrize does not include preview_xp_sha256
src/pipeline_v2/service.py:970-974: _resolve_preview_xp_fields returns (preview_xp, preview_xp_sha256) without fallback when preview_xp is truthy
src/pipeline_v2/service.py:996: empty preview_xp_sha256 appends to missing list, but this path is not exercised by any test

findings.title: test_template_registry_mounted_scope_is_explicit uses brittle list equality
findings.why_it_matters: assert human_scope['mounted_prefixes'] == ['wolfie', 'wolack'] uses exact list equality including order. The registry does not guarantee ordering semantically — if a new mounted prefix is added, or if wolfie/wolack are reordered for any reason, this test fails without any behavioral regression. The test is coupled to registry content rather than the contract property it intends to verify (that mounted prefixes are explicitly enumerated and non-authorable).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace list equality with set membership: assert set(human_scope['mounted_prefixes']) >= {'wolfie', 'wolack'}. Or check invariants: all named prefixes appear in prefix_catalog with mounted=True. This tests the contract, not the order.
evidence: tests/test_template_registry_schema.py:56-57: == ['wolfie', 'wolack'] and == ['bigbee'] assert exact list equality including order
config/template_registry.json uses a JSON array where insertion order is content-coupling

findings.title: templateSetKey empty string bypasses linkage check silently
findings.why_it_matters: At line 7019, the linkage check is conditioned on templateActions.length AND templateSetKey being truthy. When templateSetKey is an empty string (e.g., state.templateSetKey is uninitialized), the condition is false and the function proceeds to return true if all other gates pass. This means a prefix with non-empty template_actions could be reported as authorable even without a template set selected. No test covers this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a JS unit test: set state.templateSetKey to '' and prefixSpec.template_actions to a non-empty array, assert that isTemplateActionAuthorable returns false (or confirm current behavior is intentional and document it). If the intent is that no-template-set means not authorable, add a guard: if (!templateSetKey) return false before the linkage check.
evidence: web/workbench.js:7017-7019: const templateSetKey = String(state.templateSetKey || '').trim(); if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey) {...}
When templateSetKey is '' the entire linkage block is skipped and return true is reached if other gates pass
No test exercises this path

findings.title: test_template_registry_actions_are_normalized only runs against live registry
findings.why_it_matters: This test validates normalization by loading the actual live registry from disk. It does not verify that the normalizer correctly handles a multi-family registry (one containing both human and green family actions). The assertion action['skin_family'] in registry['skin_family_scope'] is always true for the current registry because all template_sets use 'human'. Adding a second family to template_sets would require no new test to pass — the test would still pass even if normalization failed to inject skin_family on that second-family action.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test for _normalize_template_registry with a synthetic two-family registry containing both human and green actions. Assert that normalized fields are correctly set for each family independently.
evidence: tests/test_template_registry_schema.py:32-36: iterates only template_sets from the live registry, which contains only human-family actions
config/template_registry.json: all template_sets entries have skin_family: 'human'

residual_risks: isTemplateActionAuthorable is the single frontend gate for all bundle action visibility. With zero unit tests, any regression in its 6 guard branches will only surface in manual testing or production.
The green/proof_only family exists in the live registry but is never exercised by any test path — neither Python nor JS tests verify that proof_only correctly suppresses action display.

Six structural validation branches in _normalize_template_registry are untested. A hand-edited or programmatically-generated malformed registry JSON could cause load_template_registry to raise an unhandled ValueError at startup (500 on all endpoints) with no test catching it first.
The templateSetKey empty-string bypass in isTemplateActionAuthorable could expose non-linked actions as authorable in uninitialized UI states, with no regression safety net.
